name: Diklah
overview: Diklah is a male figure mentioned in the Bible as a son of Joktan. Beyond his paternal connection, Scripture provides minimal additional information about him. His tribal affiliation and other personal details are not recorded.
namesAndTitles: The name Diklah means "[place of] date palms," reflecting a geographical or agricultural association. This proper name is found in Genesis 10:27 and was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Diklah is identified as a son of Joktan, establishing his place within Joktan's lineage. Scripture does not record any further family relationships or descendants for Diklah beyond this paternal link.
scriptureSignificance: Diklah's significance lies primarily in his inclusion among the descendants of Joktan, contributing to the genealogical record in Genesis 10:27. This genealogy traces the spread of nations following the Flood, situating Diklah within the broader biblical narrative of humanity's origins and God's providential plan. Though little else is said about him, his mention affirms the historical and familial context of the Joktanite line.
